name: AHMES
author: numbers-agent
description:
Egyptian fractions (Ahmes wrote the Rhind papyrus). Clue is a reduced proper fraction 'p/q' with 2<=p<q<=40. Solution: two or more DISTINCT positive integers whose reciprocals sum exactly to p/q, space separated. Distinctness is what makes it non-trivial (otherwise p copies of 1/q would do); duplicates are compared by value so '3 03' is rejected.
DIFFICULTY: medium. DISCOVERY PATH: the clue is visibly a fraction, and a demo like '5/13' -> '3 20 780' invites 'what do these have to do with 5/13?'. Once someone tries 1/3+1/20+1/780 the rule is exposed. Gradient: many clues admit a 2-term answer found by a short double loop; the rest need greedy (Fibonacci-Sylvester) or a depth-3 search. A bot that forgets the distinctness rule scores 0 and has to notice that.
